Top 60 industry groups · which are signalling · 2026-10-13

MarketSmith industry-group ranks 1–60 (2026-10-13) · each chart is MSI's own group index · last candle 09 Oct 2026 · A · Signalling 8 · B · Track 34 · C · Thin 7 · D · Unconfirmed 11
Market: Downtrend — 🔴 DOWNTREND (since 2026-10-09, Nifty -0.70%) ⚠️ Defensive stance — new buys not recommended
Not a confirmed uptrend: these groups are for the watchlist, not new entries.
How the groups are sorted — O'Neil's group rules (How to Make Money in Stocks, ch. 15 and 20), not a score. Thin: a group of 1–2 stocks is not a group move. Confirmed: at least 2 members with RS ≥ 80 ("confirmed by at least one other important stock in the same group"). A · Signalling = confirmed, not thin, and a Harris pullback in the last 3 sessions or a ▲P/▲B on the last candle. B · Track = confirmed, no signal yet. Inside each, MarketSmith's rank order. The book concentrates on the top 20 groups (badge) and never owns the bottom 20.
Price Strength = MSI's group RS rating — the same ordering as the rank. Buyer Demand (proxy) = the share of the group's stocks whose own MSI Buyer Demand (A/D) grade is A+…B−: our stand-in, because MSI's group grade is only on its web page. Leaders = members passing RS ≥ 80, EPS ≥ 70, A/D A/B (NSE tickers), strongest RS first, with a book-valid ▲P/▲G/▲B on their last candle shown beside the name (the Entry Flag Screen). Then the book's order of work: the best stock in the top group.
Signals. Harris: the Harris Pullback page's rule from upside_reversal.py — close above the 200-DMA; a candle whose low tested a support level (10/21/50/100/200 average or a prior top) or undercut the prior low, closed at or above the prior close (or reclaimed the level intraday) and in the upper half of its range, scoring at least 3 of 5 on quality; stop = that candle's low. It was tuned to miss none of Harris's own examples, so it fires often. ▲P / ▲B: entry_signals.py (definitions below). ▲G is not judged: MSI gives no open for a group index. MSI carries a bar forward as a zero-volume copy of the prior one when there was no session to compute (holidays, and the newest day before the group index updates — 28 May, 12 Oct, 13 Oct); those copies were dropped, so the last real group candle is 09 Oct 2026.
⚠️ Group volume is MSI's coarse figure (constant 100 for small groups): ▲P / ▲B are judged only where the last 60 sessions carry at least 10 distinct values, and a pocket pivot must beat the largest down day, not tie it.
⚠️ Contradiction, kept open: on 221 NSE breakouts with MSI's published group rank (about three months of data) the rank ran inverted — top-20 groups did worse than groups ranked 120+ — while the five-year study found group RS the strongest single factor (wiki: Breakout-Path-Study). None of this is a tested signal.
* #1 Retail-Major Disc Chains IN: missing from MSI's group list, so the rank comes from the stock snapshot and its group code was found by name.

Entry flags under the candles — what each one means
▲P Pocket pivot — an early buy inside a base, or off the 10-day in an uptrend, before the obvious breakout (Morales & Kacher). An up day (close above the prior close) whose volume is at least the largest down-day volume of the prior 10 sessions, closing above the 50-day average, with the day's low right at or just below the 10-day average (at most 1% above it) and the close back above the 10-day.
▲G Gap-up buy point — opens above the prior day's high; the gap from the prior close is at least 0.75× the average true range of the previous 40 sessions; volume is at least 1.5× its 50-day average; and the day's range comes within 5% of the base high. Stop = the gap day's low.
▲B Breakout — the first close above the base high (the highest high of the prior 6 months, set at least 3 weeks earlier) on volume at least 1.5× its 50-day average — the book's 50%-above-average breakout rule.
△ Not a buy — a pocket pivot or gap that breaks one of the book's rules — extended (low more than 1% above the 10-day), closed below the 10-day, below the 50-day, a downtrend (50-day falling, under the 200-day), the lower third of the base, wedging up on lighter volume, a V-shaped drop to the 20-day that never touched the 50-day, a wide and loose base (deeper than 50% or weekly swings of 10%+), or a gap extended more than 5% above the base high or still inside the base. Shown for the last 60 sessions only.
The flags are judged on SIMPLE moving averages, as in the book's charts: the 10-day (location, extended) and 50-day (above it), plus the 20-day (V-shape) and 200-day (downtrend). Every chart shows the 10- and 50-day lines — dotted where the page's own lines are EMAs.
Hover a marker to see its numbers, whether the day closed in the upper half of its range (the book calls a mid-range close weak) and whether trading was quiet before it. The thresholds freeze a discretionary book (Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple, ch. 5) into rules: reading aids, not tested signals. On NSE only the breakout-day versions are measured — gap-ups helped (42.3% vs 34.5% reached +20% in 60 days); pocket-pivot volume barely did, because 77% of breakouts have it.
